name: Shimei
title: The Benjamite Who Cursed David
summary: Shimei was a man from the tribe of Benjamin and of Saul's family. He is best known for cursing and throwing stones at King David when he fled from Absalom, and later being executed by Solomon for breaking his oath to stay in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Curses David During His Flight
keyEvents.description: When David fled from Jerusalem during Absalom's rebellion, Shimei came out, cursed him, threw stones, and called him a man of bloodshed and a troublemaker.

keyEvents.title: David Refuses Revenge
keyEvents.description: Abishai wanted to kill Shimei for his curses, but David refused and said that perhaps the Lord had commanded Shimei to curse him.

keyEvents.title: Asks David for Forgiveness
keyEvents.description: After Absalom's defeat, Shimei quickly came to meet David at the Jordan and begged forgiveness for his curses. David swore that he would not kill him.

keyEvents.title: David's Instructions to Solomon
keyEvents.description: On his deathbed, David instructed his son Solomon not to let Shimei's gray hair go down to Sheol in peace, but to show wisdom in how he dealt with him.

keyEvents.title: Ordered to Stay in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Solomon summoned Shimei and commanded him to build a house in Jerusalem and never leave the city. If he crossed the Kidron Valley, he would die. Shimei accepted the conditions.

keyEvents.title: Executed by Solomon
keyEvents.description: After three years, Shimei left Jerusalem to retrieve his escaped slaves from Gath. When Solomon learned of this, he had Benaiah execute Shimei for breaking his oath.
